transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, what really made me come in is… I’m having trouble taking in what people say. Like my wife will be talking to me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’m looking right at her, trying to listen, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really catch half of it. It’s been frustrating.
Do you feel like you’re having trouble hearing what people say?

I don’t think it’s my hearing exactly. It’s more like my wife will be telling me something—like about my cousin’s appointments or rides—and I’m looking right at her, trying to listen, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said.
Do you often have to ask people to repeat themselves because you didn’t hear the words clearly?
Not really because I didn’t hear the words clearly. It’s more that I heard them, but I didn’t process them or they didn’t stick, if that makes sense.
Has this trouble taking in what people say gotten noticeably worse compared with how you were a few years ago?

Yeah, I’d say it’s been noticeably harder over the last… about 11 months. It really started standing out after my cousin moved in with us after his surgery. Since then there’s been more to keep track of, and I’ve noticed I’m missing more of what people are telling me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time lately?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed much of the time. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down most days.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
Not a lot, no. I mean, I worry about normal stuff here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s been taking over or anything lately.
Looking back to when you were a child, did you often have the same kind of trouble paying attention when people were talking to you?

Yeah, I think so. Even back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always daydreaming. I’d leave homework in my desk and needed reminders to finish my classwork.
Do these attention lapses also cause problems for you in places other than at home, such as at work or when managing daily tasks?

Yes, it does. At home it’s caused some tension because my wife feels like she can’t always count on me with helping take care of my cousin. And with the catering jobs I help with, I’ve had to double-check things or redo small tasks so orders or details don’t get mixed up.
Do you often lose things you need, like keys, paperwork, or your phone?

Yeah, I do. I’ll set my keys or my phone down somewhere and then I’m wandering around the house trying to remember where. Same with catering receipts or even garden clippers. It’s usually not gone, but I lose ten minutes retracing my steps.
Have you noticed needing the TV or radio louder than other people prefer?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed needing the TV or radio louder than other people. If anything, I just keep it at a normal level.
Have you been forgetting things more than you used to?

Yeah, I think so. Lately I’ve been forgetting things I meant to do, like calling the doctor’s office back or picking up a prescription. I’ve also cut it close or left late for my cousin’s appointments because I forgot what time I needed to get going.
Are you having trouble managing your bills or finances?

Not bills so much, no. It’s more that I forget regular things I meant to do, like calling the doctor’s office back or picking up a prescription, or I’ll lose track and leave late for one of my cousin’s appointments.
Did your attention and memory problems get noticeably worse after a stroke, head injury, or another major medical illness?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had a stroke or a head injury or anything like that that I can point to. It’s more just something I’ve noticed gradually, I guess.
Do you have trouble remembering conversations or events from the last few days?

Sometimes, yeah. It’s not so much that I forget a whole event, but my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’m looking right at her… then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said.
Have other people noticed that your memory has gotten worse?

Yeah, my wife has noticed it. It’s been causing some tension at home because she feels like she can’t really count on me as much with my cousin’s care. And with catering stuff, I’ve had to double-check things or redo small tasks so they don’t get mixed up.
Have you started having trouble making plans or organizing tasks that used to be easy for you?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed some big change where planning suddenly got hard. I mean, I can still make a plan if I sit down and focus on it, but I don’t know if it’s worse than before.
Have your memory problems been steadily getting worse over the past year?

I’d say it’s been noticeably harder for about 11 months now, since my cousin moved in with us after surgery. I don’t know if it’s steadily getting worse every month, but that’s when I really started noticing it.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’ve been struggling to find words when I’m talking. Maybe every once in a while like anyone does, but nothing that stands out to me.
Have these attention problems been present fairly consistently throughout your life, even before the past year?

Yes, I think so. Even when I was a kid, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright but always daydreaming. I’d leave homework in my desk and need reminders to finish my classwork. So it doesn’t feel like it’s completely new, just more noticeable lately.
Has a doctor told you that you have any medical condition affecting your brain or nervous system?
No, not that I know of. No doctor has told me I have anything affecting my brain or nervous system.
